primitives.name: Expected Possession Value
primitives.verbatim_quote: Per-event reward ΔEPV = difference of neighboring EPV values (turnover penalized twice: -EPV(ci+1) - EPV(ci); goal scored rewards 1 - EPV(ci) - EPV(ci+1)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'EPV': 'dimensionless, expected value of possession at time t', 'ΔEPV': 'dimensionless change in EPV between events'}
primitives.assumptions: Markovian evolution of possession states; linear additive reward structure for turnarounds and goals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession ends without clear outcome (e.g., foul, offside).

layer2.mapping: EDV in GSE mirrors EPV in soccer, substituting xP for xG and defining drives as possessions.
layer2.telemetry: RMSE and MAE of next-season PCR predictions against baseline carry-forward.

primitives.name: Player Control Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: Custom per-player-weighted log-loss (xG) and MSE (EPV) dividing each shot's loss by the player's appearance count to de-overweight overrepresented players.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'PCR': 'dimensionless, normalized control impact per minute', 'ΔEPV': 'change in EPV from pass/carry event', 'min(p)': 'total minutes played by player p'}
primitives.assumptions: Control actions contribute linearly to EPV gain; normalization by minutes ensures fair comparison across activity levels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Players with <100 minutes or high variance in action quality.

layer2.mapping: PCR maps to player skill in GSE’s contested-play framework via per-play ΔEDV attribution.
layer2.telemetry: Transfer bias-adjusted PCR (PCR_adj) used in predictive modeling of next-season performance.

primitives.name: Modified Glicko-2 Duel Skill
primitives.verbatim_quote: -duel EPV, ground average-duel EPV, and two duel EPV models including player ratings.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'rating': 'Glicko-2 rating scale (dimensionless)', 'Δratings': 'normalized rating change between leagues'}
primitives.assumptions: Skill differences follow normal distribution; rating updates reflect match outcomes and uncertainty.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low-frequency duel interactions or extreme rating shifts.

layer2.mapping: GSE's duel-skill analog uses modified Glicko-2 to assess contested-play effectiveness, adapting to NFL player matchups.
layer2.telemetry: Model accuracy in predicting win probability of contested plays based on adjusted duel ratings.

The core insight is that EPV models control and duel actions as stochastic processes evolving over time. Each action contributes a ΔEPV, which is computed as the difference in expected value before and after the event. Turnovers are penalized twice because they represent a loss of possession, while goals reward the full potential of the subsequent possession. This leads to a recursive structure where EPV depends on future outcomes, modeled via a product form involving xG probabilities. The paper introduces a time-decayed version of EPV to better capture temporal relevance. For player skill estimation, PCR aggregates these contributions into a per-minute score, adjusted for appearances to prevent overrepresentation. Transfer bias is corrected using Δratings derived from league-level Glicko-2 adjustments. These primitives form a dualism: one layer estimates static skill (PCR, duel ratings), another models dynamic possession flow (EPV). Failure modes include overfitting due to sparse data, misalignment of xG/xP assumptions, and lack of temporal consistency in skill ratings.
